bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or have received a salary offer, the first step is to work out your annual gross pay. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. That gives you annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, so a full-time worker on that rate earns about $52,254 per year before tax and super.

### Why 38 Hours and What About Fortnights?

The 38-hour week is the standard for full-time employment under most awards and the National Employment Standards. If you work part-time or casual, your hours may differ. Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your actual weekly hours. Once you have your weekly pay, you can double it to get your fortnightly amount. Fortnightly pay is common in Australia, and knowing it helps with budgeting and comparing salary offers.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most workers are covered by an industry or occupation award, which often sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Hospitality Award or the General Retail Industry Award have specific pay levels. Award rates can include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you find the right award, but remember that the calculator on this site uses the base rate you enter – it does not automatically apply award conditions.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. The casual rate for the National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour. When using our [timesheet](/), there is a checkbox to add the 25% casual loading. Never type a rate that already includes loading – let the calculator apply it. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% from 1 July 2026, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time worker on the minimum wage, that means an extra $6,270 in super per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution your employer makes.

### Tax, Medicare, and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026–27: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above that. Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a single person earning $52,254 (minimum wage full-time), the tax would be about $5,100 and Medicare about $1,045, leaving a take-home pay of roughly $46,109. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page explains this in more detail. Note that the calculator uses the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here.

### Can I Salary Sacrifice into My Super?

Yes, you can salary sacrifice into your super. This means you agree with your employer to put some of your pre-tax salary directly into your super fund. Salary sacrifice reduces your taxable income, so you pay less tax now, but the money is locked away until retirement. It is important to stay within the concessional contribution cap (currently $30,000 per year, including the 12% super guarantee). Salary sacrifice is not included in our annual pay estimate because it is an individual arrangement. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Using the Timesheet and Reference Tables

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page. You enter your base hourly rate, and if you are casual, tick the casual loading box. The calculator then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax, Medicare, and super. For a quick reference, see our [reference tables](/data) which list the National Minimum Wage, award rates (as averages), and ABS earnings data. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026. That is an average across all industries and states, not a median for your specific job. Similarly, the all-employees total earnings average is $1,579.20 per week, which includes part-time workers.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
